newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan Central Bank cuts discount rate to 8.25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Jordan Central Bank cuts discount rate to 8.25 pct.

text.p: Jordan's Central Bank on Monday cut its benchmark discount rate to 8.25 percent from 8.50 percent, the first rate change in nearly eight years, after foreign currency reserves soared to record levels.
Repurchase rates on certificates of deposit were also cut to 9.75 percent from 10.00 percent, the bank said.
The cuts are also in line with the fall in yields on CDs, a key interest rate indicator, since the bank introduced competitive bidding to its CD auctions last month as part of capital market reforms.

CD rates had been unchanged for a year and a half but since the first two competitive auctions the average yield on three-month paper has fallen to 8.52 percent from a fixed 9.25 percent and the yield on six-month paper has gone down to 8.75 percent from 9.50 percent.
The Central Bank has been encouraged to lower yields on CDs by the rise in net foreign currency reserves to record levels, close to a 1997 target of $1.050 billion, bankers said.

The competitive market-dictated CD auction system enables yields to move more in line with supply and demand, but monetary authorities will be able to inject or drain liquidity to ensure that interest rates do not leave the target band, officials said.
The Central Bank's interest rate policy is to make dinar-denominated assets attractive and to prevent a flow of dinars into dollar-denominated assets.

Bankers say lower interest rates will act as a stimulant to growth and inject more liquidity into the stock market, which has suffered from a shortage of cash as high interest rates drove small investors to higher-yield bank deposits.

They say the monetary authorities will aim to keep at least a three to four percentage point differential between dinar and dollar interest yields to prevent a switch into the U.S. currency that could undermine exchange rate stability. -- Amman newsroom +9626 623 776
